# FDG5076

> DO NOT put extension methods in the same namespace as the extended type unless the intention is to add methods to interfaces, for generic type restriction, or for dependency management.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 5.6 Extension Methods.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG5076
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: draft

Message: Move the extension method '{0}' out of the namespace of the type '{1}' it extends

FDG5076 reports an externally visible extension method declared in the namespace of the type it extends when that type is declared in the same assembly, is not an interface, and the method does not restrict a generic type: the extended type is not generic, or every type argument is a type parameter of the method without constraints. The three exceptions of the text are interfaces, generic type restriction and dependency management; for the last the body says the extension methods are in a different assembly, and since symbols do not show why an assembly extends another assembly's type in that type's namespace, extended types from other assemblies are not reported at all. Moving a public class to another namespace changes the public API, so the fix is breaking.

## From the book

Of course, in the case of dependency management, the type with the extension methods would be in a different assembly.
